this file by generate.py and must never be hand-edited.
Assembled 2026-08-23 from six independent reads of the PRD, the
ADRs and the Bible's 200 acceptance criteria.

meta.currency: configuration - INR with minor-unit ratio 100 (SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01). The ratio is NEVER baked into a column name, comment or constraint: it is a one-way door, because reinterpreting the unit later rewrites what every past customer paid.
meta.timezone: configuration - Asia/Kolkata (SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01, RULED). Every instant is timestamptz in UTC and is rendered in the cinema's zone (FR-ADR-018).
meta.primary_keys: bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY on every table (FR-ADR-017). UUID is rejected by name in that ADR, and the deciding argument is this schema's most contended index: two 8-byte integers make a 16-byte key where two UUIDs make a 32-byte one.

seat_guarantee.why: The product's central promise, and the half that may not be waived. TOTAL, with no WHERE: S-XCT-02/03/04 read pg_get_constraintdef back and require no predicate, and S-PAY-09 requires exactly one unique index on the table. A cancelled booking's seats are therefore NOT freed, which is the ruled answer - both FR-ADR-024 and P-PAY-11 carry the same revisit trigger: if cancellation is ever added, this constraint has to be revisited FIRST.

tables_beyond_bible.seat_category: FR-ADR-016 - a lookup table, not a database enum, because a fourth category should cost an INSERT and not a migration, and because the category carries a price uplift an enum cannot hold. seat.seat_category_id is NOT NULL, so seat cannot exist without it.
tables_beyond_bible.manager_screen_assignment: FR-ADR-011, P-ADM-17. UNIQUE (user_id, screen_id), asserted by name by S-ADM-18.
tables_beyond_bible.movie_genre: the many-to-many join between movie and genre (P-ADM-23).
tables_beyond_bible.genre: P-ADM-23, one of four admin-maintained vocabularies.

bible_reference_exceptions.screen.rows: a JSON response field, not a column - the grid extent is derived per response (P-BRW-08); screen has no rows column
bible_reference_exceptions.screen.name: prose naming the column of `screen` in a sentence, not a qualified SQL reference
bible_reference_exceptions.seat.is_active: prose; the column exists on seat and resolves normally, listed only because the Bible writes it dotted in prose
bible_reference_exceptions.booking.py: a Python filename, not a table reference
bible_reference_exceptions.screen.exploded: a DELIBERATELY INVALID audit action. S-ADM-02 constructs AuditAction from this string and requires ValueError, proving the vocabulary is closed. Declaring it as a real action would break the very test it exists for.
bible_reference_exceptions.showtime.sales_closed: a JSON field in the seatmap response, not a column. The sales cut-off has NO column: it is starts_at + SALES_CUTOFF_MINUTES, and S-BRW-10 and S-SEA-11 both assert the column's absence.

roles.name: frontrow_owner
roles.why: owns every table and runs migrations. NEVER the role the application connects as.
roles.cite: SRC-002 (build against a restricted role) - the role NAMES are a [JUDGMENT CALL]: no document in the repository contains a single CREATE ROLE, GRANT or REVOKE.

roles.name: frontrow_app
roles.why: the application role. Not a superuser and not the owner. The two-role split is FORCED, not stylistic: S-XCT-07 asserts that table_privileges for audit_log and current_user returns EXACTLY two rows. Observed on PostgreSQL 16.14 - a table's OWNER sees seven (DELETE, INSERT, REFERENCES, SELECT, TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, UPDATE), so a single-role design cannot satisfy that criterion at all. With a separate owner the same query returns exactly INSERT and SELECT.

tables.name: audit_log
tables.purpose: One append-only row per privileged write, inserted in the same database transaction as the change itself, recording who, when, which action, which row, and the changed fields before and after.
tables.cite: P-XCT-03 · E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · FR-ADR-019

columns.name: id
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 and P-ADM-19 and FR-ADR-019 all spell it '`bigint` identity' · P-RPT-11 step 3 (cursor on `id`, ordered descending)
columns.note: THE ONLY PRIMARY KEY IN THIS CLUSTER A DOCUMENT GIVES A GENERATION MECHANISM FOR. EP-RPT-04's `cursor` is a positive integer audit row id and is a BOUND, not a lookup: a well-formed id naming no row returns 200, never 404.

columns.name: occurred_at
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · S-XCT-06 (`SELECT data_type ... column_name='occurred_at'` returns 'timestamp with time zone')
columns.note: UTC. S-XCT-06 additionally asserts the value the APPLICATION BINDS is an aware datetime whose utcoffset() is zero — so it is written by the application from the injected clock, not by a database default.

columns.name: actor_user_id
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · P-XCT-03 server-side validation · S-XCT-06 (`is_nullable` returns NO, and one foreign key row in pg_constraint)
columns.note: NEVER A ROLE NAME AND NEVER A SERVICE ACCOUNT — both substitutes are forbidden in terms. The seed script is the ONLY exemption from the same-transaction audit rule anywhere in the product, precisely because at its earliest writes no user row exists to point at (P-XCT-30); it writes zero audit rows and no application code path inherits that exemption.

columns.name: actor_role
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · S-XCT-06 (asserted still to read 'admin' after user 17's role is changed to manager)
columns.note: THE ROLE THE ACTOR HELD AT THE TIME, COPIED RATHER THAN JOINED. Never resolved by a join at read time. NO DOCUMENT STATES THE COLUMN TYPE — `text` is reported rather than `enum:user_role` because the point of the column is that it is a frozen copy, and a shared enum type ties historical rows to a live vocabulary. See gaps; this is the merge owner's call.

columns.name: action
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19's controlled vocabulary table (the single source of the strings for the whole product) · FR-ADR-019
columns.note: A CLOSED controlled vocabulary, enumerated by P-ADM-19 and by no one else. ENFORCED IN THE APPLICATION, NOT IN THE DATABASE: S-ADM-02 requires a closed Python enum `AuditAction`, S-XCT-07 requires a module-level tuple `AUDIT_ACTIONS` in backend/app/domain/audit.py, and a non-member is refused at a boundary check BEFORE THE TRANSACTION OPENS (asserted by a statement listener recording zero statements). No document asks for a database CHECK or a Postgres enum, so none is proposed. The string already got wrong once: a base-price change is `showtime.base_price_changed`; `showtime.price_changed` is NOT a member and never has been, although FR-ADR-019's own example text still shows it.

columns.name: entity_type
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19
columns.note: The table the change landed on. Values seen in the vocabulary table: movie, showtime, seat_category, cinema, screen, seat, user, manager_screen_assignment, language, certification, genre, format.

columns.name: entity_id
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19
columns.note: The primary key of the changed row. NO FOREIGN KEY MAY EXIST ON THIS COLUMN — S-ADM-18 asserts the FK count on audit_log.entity_id is 0, because for `manager.screen_unassigned` it deliberately names a row that no longer exists and 'a column that resolves by lying about what it points at is worse than one that honestly points at something gone'. Nothing may join it to a live table for that action. Width is not stated by any document — see gaps.

columns.name: before
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · P-XCT-03 server-side validation
columns.note: ONLY THE FIELDS THAT CHANGED, never a whole-row snapshot (S-XCT-06 asserts jsonb_object_keys(before) counts 1 for a single-field change). NULL FOR A CREATION. Carries no credential (`password_hash`, `password_version` excluded from every entity_type='user' row), no card-shaped key, and no poster bytes — only the S3 object key.

columns.name: after
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19
columns.note: Null for a withdrawal that changes nothing else — including `manager.screen_unassigned`, whose `before` carries exactly `{"user_id": n, "screen_id": n}`. Same credential and card-data exclusions as `before`. Returned VERBATIM by EP-RPT-04 and never unit-converted.

columns.name: request_id
columns.cite: E8 S7.3 · P-ADM-19 · P-XCT-03 happy path step 4 and preconditions · FR-ADR-056
columns.note: The request id from the log context, so an audit row joins to the log lines. Matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}$ (S-XCT-06). NO DOCUMENT STATES ITS NULLABILITY EXPLICITLY — reported NOT NULL because P-XCT-03's precondition requires it to be available before the transaction opens and every audit row is written from a request; flag it if the merge disagrees.

foreign_keys.cite: P-XCT-03 ('non-null foreign key to the acting user') · S-XCT-06 (one pg_constraint FK row on audit_log) · S-XCT-09 (every FK in the schema is confdeltype 'r')

tables.name: booking
tables.purpose: One confirmed purchase: one user, one showtime, one captured payment, one unique customer-facing reference, and a stored total.
tables.cite: E3 P-PAY-01 · E3 P-PAY-10 step 7 · FR-ADR-014 · FR-ADR-039

columns.name: id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-020 (idempotency_record.id is 'bigint identity') · E6 P-ADM-19 audit_log id table ('bigint identity') · S-XCT-08 ('booking_id 9008')
columns.note: NOT uuid. No document in this project uses a uuid primary key anywhere; the two places a PK type is spelled out both read 'bigint identity', and every id in every criterion and every endpoint body is a small integer (booking_id 9008, user_id 4471, showtime_id 7/41/77, seat_id 312/402). EP-PAY-01's 201 body declares booking_id as 'integer'. The brief's uuid default is overridden here by the sources, as the brief permits.

columns.name: reference
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-01 · FR-ADR-015 · S-TKT-01
columns.note: THE COLUMN IS NAMED `reference`, not reference_code and not booking_reference. Exactly 8 characters, uppercase, drawn from 23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ, with NO `FR-` prefix and NO hyphens stored (those are presentation only). `SELECT length(reference), reference = upper(reference) FROM booking WHERE id=:b` must return 8, true. NO CHECK CONSTRAINT ON THE ALPHABET and no length CHECK is added here: OPEN-REFCHAR-01 is reserved (irreversible) and expires at Phase 4; narrowing the alphabet or adding a check character is the client's call. P-TKT-01 states the validation is performed in application code before insert, and that the UNIQUE constraint (not the alphabet) is the guard.

columns.name: user_id
columns.cite: S-ACC-10 (verbatim: 'booking.user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT') · FR-ADR-014 · E4 EP-TKT-01 authorisation_rule
columns.note: Type spelled `integer` (not bigint) by S-ACC-10. It must match users(id); see notes[] — the merge owner must reconcile this with booking.id being bigint. The owner is always taken from the JWT, never from the request body (S-ACC-10 route-table walk).

columns.name: showtime_id
columns.cite: E7 P-RPT-03 formula ('JOIN booking b ON b.showtime_id = st.id') · S-PAY-06 · S-PAY-15 · EP-PAY-01 201 body
columns.note: Integer, matching E6 P-ADM-14's showtime_seat.showtime_id 'integer'.

columns.name: payment_id
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 ('booking.payment_id points at payment.id, not the reverse') · E3 P-PAY-01 ('no state in which a booking exists without a captured payment') · S-PAY-05 · S-SCP-12 · E7 P-RPT-12
columns.note: THE DIRECTION IS LOAD-BEARING AND SETTLED IN FIVE PLACES. payment carries NO booking_id column: the payment row is inserted at P-PAY-10 step 6 and the booking at step 7, so a payment.booking_id could not be satisfied at insert time. NOT NULL is what makes 'no booking without a payment record' a database fact rather than a test; see gaps[] for the half that is not expressible (the payment being in a terminal captured state).

columns.name: total_paise
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-04 · FR-ADR-039 · S-PAY-01 · S-SEA-16
columns.note: Integer minor unit. The sum of the ALREADY-ROUNDED per-seat prices; the total is never itself rounded. Deliberately denormalised (FR-ADR-039) — the equality total_paise = SUM(booking_seat.price_paise) is asserted at write time as a TEST, explicitly NOT as a database constraint, because a constraint would need a trigger. The minor-unit ratio 100 is CURRENCY_MINOR_UNIT_RATIO, a named configuration value, and appears in no column name, comment or constraint.

columns.name: status
columns.cite: FR-ADR-013 · E3 P-PAY-12 · E7 P-RPT-03 ("b.status = 'confirmed'") · S-PAY-11 · S-SCP-14
columns.note: EXCLUDED IS NOT BLOCKED (SRC-001 §6.6). Written exactly once, by the confirm insert, to 'confirmed'. No v1 endpoint reads or writes it; it appears in no v1 request or response schema. `SELECT DISTINCT status FROM booking` must return exactly one row after the whole suite. TYPE IS UNSOURCED — no document says whether this is a Postgres enum or text, and no document names any value other than 'confirmed'. Declaring an enum here would mean naming a 'cancelled' value, which is the reserved question OPEN-CANCEL-01/OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01. Reported as a gap rather than decided.

columns.name: cancelled_at
columns.cite: FR-ADR-013 · E3 P-PAY-12 · E4 P-TKT-09 · S-PAY-11 · S-SCP-14
columns.note: EXCLUDED IS NOT BLOCKED (SRC-001 §6.6). Stays null for every row v1 ever creates: `SELECT count(*) FROM booking WHERE cancelled_at IS NOT NULL` returns 0. Exists because adding a column to a table already holding real bookings is a migration on live data with a backfill nobody can verify. S-SCP-04 explicitly permits it while banning refund/tax/fee/discount/points/used_at names on this table.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: E8 P-XCT-04 preconditions ('Every table carries created_at') · S-XCT-08 ('SELECT b.id, b.user_id, b.created_at ...') · S-XCT-09 · E5 P-ACC-11 ordering tie-breaker
columns.note: UTC instant. Serialised to customers with the CINEMA ROW's UTC offset (never Z, never a hardcoded zone) — EP-PAY-01 returns it as created_at, EP-ACC-07 as booked_at. It is also an ordering tie-breaker for the bookings list (S-ACC-12: upcoming ordered by showtime.starts_at asc, booking.created_at desc, booking.id asc).

unique.cite: E4 P-TKT-01 preconditions ('The booking.reference column exists with a UNIQUE constraint on it') · FR-ADR-015 · S-TKT-01
unique.why: The reference is the customer's ONLY proof of purchase and their only way into the hall. Generation draws 8 random characters and RELIES ON THIS CONSTRAINT as the collision guard, retrying up to five times and then failing the request with 500 rather than looping. P-TKT-01: 'The arithmetic is not the guard; the constraint is.'

columns.cite: project id convention: FR-ADR-020, E6 P-ADM-19 ('bigint identity')
columns.note: NO DOCUMENT NAMES A PRIMARY KEY FOR THIS TABLE. See gaps[] — the merge owner must choose between a surrogate id and a composite PK on (booking_id, seat_id). Nothing in any criterion selects a booking_seat id.

columns.name: booking_id
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-10 step 7 · S-PAY-03 · S-PAY-07 · S-SCP-13 · S-XCT-08 · E7 P-RPT-03 formula
columns.note: Every criterion in the Bible that reads a booked seat filters on booking_id.

columns.name: showtime_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-024 · E3 P-PAY-11 · S-XCT-01 · S-XCT-02 · S-XCT-03 · S-PAY-09 · S-SEA-13 · S-SEA-16 · S-SEA-18 · S-SEA-20
columns.note: DENORMALISED FROM booking.showtime_id ON PURPOSE. It exists so the oversell unique constraint can be (showtime_id, seat_id) — the guarantee has to be at seat granularity across the whole showtime, not per booking. At least nine acceptance criteria run `SELECT count(*) FROM booking_seat WHERE showtime_id=? AND seat_id=?` directly. Nothing in the documents states how showtime_id is kept consistent with booking.showtime_id.

columns.name: seat_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-024 · S-PAY-09 ('seat_id is an integer foreign key and seat_label carries the human form such as F7; a query comparing seat_id to a label string raises invalid input syntax for type integer against a correct schema') · S-XCT-08 · S-XCT-34
columns.note: INTEGER, NOT A LABEL. The human-readable form (F7, C12) lives on the `seat` table and is joined for display (S-XCT-08: `JOIN seat s ON s.id = bs.seat_id`); it is never copied onto booking_seat.

columns.name: price_paise
columns.cite: FR-ADR-039 · E3 P-PAY-05 · S-PAY-01 · S-SEA-16 · E7 P-RPT-03
columns.note: The rounded per-seat price the customer actually paid, snapshotted at HOLD acquisition (not at confirm) and copied onto this row; never recomputed by any display path, receipt, bookings list or dashboard. Integer minor unit, bigint.

columns.name: base_price_paise_applied
columns.cite: FR-ADR-039 · E3 P-PAY-05 (column table) · S-PAY-03 · S-SEA-16
columns.note: The showtime base price that produced price_paise. Stored so the figure is auditable — SRC-001 §7.6 requires the system to answer for its own records; storing only price_paise makes it impossible to tell a 33.33% uplift on Rs 275.00 from a 20% uplift on something else. Money column: bigint, name ends _paise.

columns.name: uplift_basis_points_applied
columns.cite: FR-ADR-039 · E3 P-PAY-05 (column table) · S-PAY-03 · S-SEA-16
columns.note: The seat category's uplift in basis points at the time of booking. NOT a money column — its name deliberately does not end in _paise, and S-PAY-01's assertion (money columns on booking/booking_seat/payment ending in _paise are EXACTLY total_paise, price_paise, base_price_paise_applied, amount_paise) depends on that.

columns.name: seat_category_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-039 ('the category at the time of booking, copied, not joined for display') · E3 P-PAY-05 ('integer, positive, non-null') · S-PAY-03
columns.note: Copied rather than joined, so a later category rename or re-categorisation cannot rewrite what a past receipt says.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: E8 P-XCT-04 ('Every table carries created_at') · S-XCT-09
columns.note: S-XCT-09 asserts information_schema returns zero public tables lacking created_at.

unique.why: THE PRODUCT. The second half of the double-booking guarantee, and the half that may not be waived at any confidence for any reason (waiving a quality check is reserved to the client, CONSTITUTION Art III.8). TOTAL, NOT PARTIAL — the documents settle this explicitly and in five places. FR-ADR-024: 'The constraint is total, not partial. No WHERE status <> cancelled clause.' P-PAY-11: 'The constraint is total, not partial. There is no WHERE status <> cancelled clause, because P-PAY-12 rules out cancellation in v1. If cancellation is ever added, this constraint has to be revisited first — a cancelled booking holding a seat forever is what a total constraint would then produce.' Three criteria assert the absence of a WHERE clause directly against the catalogue: S-XCT-02 and S-XCT-03 read pg_get_constraintdef and require no WHERE; S-XCT-04 requires `SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'booking_seat'` to contain no WHERE and requires the guard to be a CONSTRAINT rather than a partial index; S-PAY-09 requires pg_indexes to return EXACTLY ONE unique index on this table. So a cancelled booking's seats are NOT freed, and that is the ruled behaviour, not an oversight. It must be created in the SAME Alembic revision as create_table('booking_seat') (S-XCT-04), so no window exists in which a seat row can be written without it, and no later revision may drop it.

unique.cite: FR-ADR-020 ('Unique constraint on (user_id, idempotency_key)') · E3 P-PAY-09 · EP-PAY-01 idempotency block · S-PAY-06
unique.why: THE CHECK AND THE ACT IN ONE STATEMENT. The row is inserted FIRST, in the same transaction as the booking, before any other work. The insert either succeeds — this request owns the key — or it violates the constraint, in which case this request is a duplicate. There is no check-then-act window, which is exactly the trap GOTCHAS.md records: 'An idempotency key stored after the work is done is not idempotent. Two simultaneous retries both check, both find nothing, both book.' The three duplicate behaviours are the whole set: winner completed -> replay the stored response_body with the original status code; winner in_progress -> 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT with Retry-After (never a wait, because holding a connection open ties up one of ~110 on a db.t3.micro); fingerprint differs -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.

columns.name: payload
columns.cite: FR-ADR-031 Decision ('`payload` (`jsonb`)'); E4 P-TKT-04 payload table
columns.note: Key set is fixed per topic and is exhaustive. `receipt.send`: booking_id, dispatch_seq, request_id, message_version. `password_reset.send`: user_id, reset_token_id, request_id, message_version. 'No customer data travels in the payload — no email address, no seat list, no amount' (P-TKT-04, FR-ADR-059). NO CARD DATA anywhere. columns.cite: FR-ADR-031 Decision ('`status` (`pending` / `sent`)'); E4 P-TKT-04 Preconditions and happy path steps 1, 3, 4

columns.note: Set only when the queue accepted the message. Bible S-TKT-06: 'with the queue reachable the same confirm leaves that row `sent` with sent_at non-null'. Never cleared; `sent` rows are kept forever as the record that the receipt was dispatched (P-TKT-04 step 5, FR-ADR-012).

columns.name: last_error
columns.cite: FR-ADR-031 Decision ('`attempts`, `last_error`'); E4 P-TKT-04 Preconditions
columns.note: The column is required by two documents but NO specification states when it is written. P-TKT-04 exception row 5 says only that the relay 'logs at ERROR and retries on the next loop; the row stays `pending` and `attempts` increments' — it does not say last_error is set. Reported as specified, with the write rule listed in gaps.

tables.name: password_reset_token
tables.purpose: One row per password-reset request: the SHA-256 of a token that is never stored, its expiry, whether it was spent, and the two separate columns that track the worker's send of the reset email.
tables.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 and its two-column table · P-ACC-08 step 4 · E4 P-TKT-12

columns.name: id
columns.cite: P-TKT-12 server-side validation — '`reset_token_id`: integer, positive, existing' · S-TKT-15 (`WHERE id=:t`)
columns.note: The queue message carries this id and NEVER the token. No document states the generation mechanism.

columns.name: user_id
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 ('a `password_reset_token` row holding `user_id` ...') · S-ACC-07 (`WHERE user_id=:id`)
columns.note: The account the link is for. P-TKT-12 validates that the message's `user_id` matches this column; a mismatch is dead-lettered, never sent.

columns.name: token_sha256
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 ('`token_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the token, hex)') · S-ACC-07
columns.note: SHA-256 hex of a 43-character URL-safe token drawn from 32 CSPRNG bytes. ONLY THE HASH IS STORED — 'somebody who can read the table cannot mint a session from it'. P-ACC-08 step 1 looks the row up by this value. S-ACC-07 asserts the 43 characters appear in `SELECT password_reset_token::text`, in the 202 body and in DEBUG-level stdout NOWHERE. DO NOT ADD A PLAINTEXT TOKEN COLUMN — see gaps, OPEN-RESETTOKEN-01.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 and its worked example ('`expires_at = created_at + PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS`')
columns.note: PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS default 1800 (a [JUDGMENT CALL], configuration, not a ruled number). Compared against the INJECTED clock in UTC (FR-ADR-018). The 1800 must not appear as a literal in a constraint or a message — every customer-visible '30 minutes' is rendered from the variable.

columns.name: used_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 · P-ACC-08 step 4 · S-SCP-04 ('The password_reset_token.used_at column is explicitly excluded from the check and must still exist')
columns.note: THE THIRD AND SEPARATE TIMESTAMP: it records the CUSTOMER SPENDING the token and has nothing to do with the send. The single-use guarantee is the conditional update `UPDATE password_reset_token SET used_at = :now WHERE id = :id AND used_at IS NULL` affecting exactly one row inside the password-change transaction — not a prior read. P-ACC-07 step 3 also sets it on every outstanding unused token for that user, so at most one live token exists per account. NOTE THE NEAR-MISS: S-SCP-04's excluded-column sweep bans `used_at` on `booking` and MUST NOT trip over this column.

columns.name: email_claimed_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 and its column table ('a worker is holding this send job') · E4 P-TKT-12 step 2 and exceptions 3a, 4, 6
columns.note: A CLAIM, NOT A RECORD OF DELIVERY. Set by the conditional claim; CLEARED BACK TO NULL on an SES refusal or a SES_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS timeout (`UPDATE password_reset_token SET email_claimed_at = NULL WHERE id = :id AND email_sent_at IS NULL`); and overtaken by the age branch `email_claimed_at < now() - :stale_interval` (RECEIPT_CLAIM_STALE_SECONDS, 900) when a worker dies before it can clear anything. These are ONE reclaim mechanism with a fast path, not two.

columns.name: email_sent_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 and its column table ('an email went out … never cleared by anything') · E4 P-TKT-12 step 4 and exception 3
columns.note: TERMINAL. Set only after SES accepts, and NEVER CLEARED BY ANYTHING — that is what makes a duplicate credential email impossible even if the queue delete fails and SQS redelivers a day later (S-TKT-15 asserts a redelivery 24 injected hours later makes 0 SES calls).

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-07 step 5 (the row holds `created_at`) · FR-ADR-018 · S-XCT-09 (every table carries created_at)
columns.note: See gaps: S-ACC-07 asserts `expires_at = created_at + 1800 seconds FROM THE INJECTED CLOCK`, which a database-side `now()` default cannot satisfy under an injected test clock.

foreign_keys.cite: S-XCT-09 — `SELECT conname, confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE contype = 'f' AND confdeltype <> 'r'` returns 0 ROWS, i.e. EVERY foreign key in the schema is RESTRICT · P-XCT-04 · FR-ADR-012
foreign_keys.name: fk_password_reset_token__user_id

indexes.cite: P-ACC-08 step 1 ('hashes the submitted token with SHA-256 and looks the row up by that hash') · P-ACC-08's rate-limit rationale ('it bounds the indexed lookup per guess')
indexes.why: The confirm endpoint's only lookup. DERIVED FROM THE NAMED QUERY — no document declares this index, and no document says whether it is unique (see gaps).
indexes.name: ix_password_reset_token__token_sha256

indexes.cite: P-ACC-07 step 3 ('marks every outstanding unused reset token for that user as used') · S-ACC-07 (`SELECT count(*) FROM password_reset_token WHERE user_id=:id AND used_at IS NULL`)
indexes.why: The per-user sweep that keeps at most one live token per account. DERIVED FROM THE NAMED QUERY, not declared by any document.
indexes.name: ix_password_reset_token__user_id

tables.name: payment
tables.purpose: One row per booking ATTEMPT recording the simulated provider's state machine, the amount captured, the transition instants, and the idempotency key that produced it.
tables.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 · FR-ADR-041

columns.name: id
columns.cite: project id convention: FR-ADR-020, E6 P-ADM-19 ('bigint identity') · referenced by booking.payment_id
columns.note: The payment row is inserted BEFORE the booking row (P-PAY-10 step 6 then step 7), so its id must be available to the booking insert.

columns.name: state
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 · FR-ADR-041 · E7 P-RPT-03 ('payment.state is one of pending, authorized, captured, failed') · S-PAY-11 ('SELECT unnest(enum_range(NULL::payment_state))') · S-SCP-12 ('the column is state')
columns.note: THE COLUMN IS NAMED `state`, NOT `status`. Two Bible criteria get this wrong — see notes[]. It is a real Postgres enum type named payment_state: S-PAY-11 asserts `enum_range(NULL::payment_state)` returns exactly four rows and no 'refunded'. Transitions are enforced in code: capture from pending is rejected (InvalidPaymentTransition), and failed is terminal. closed vocabulary, enforced by a CHECK rather than a PostgreSQL enum type

columns.name: amount_paise
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 ('carrying the state, the amount in paise, the transition timestamps and the Idempotency-Key') · FR-ADR-041 · S-PAY-01 · S-PAY-05 · S-PAY-10
columns.note: The fourth and last money column in this cluster. S-PAY-10: payment.amount_paise, booking.total_paise and the figure on the checkout total are all the same integer, and `SELECT sum(price_paise) FROM booking_seat WHERE booking_id=B` also returns it. Never a float, never NUMERIC(x,2).

columns.name: idempotency_key
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 ('One payment row per booking attempt, carrying ... the Idempotency-Key that produced it') · FR-ADR-041 · S-PAY-05 · S-PAY-15
columns.note: NOT UNIQUE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. S-PAY-15 proves it: the same FAIL_-prefixed key sent twice leaves `SELECT count(*) FROM payment WHERE state='failed'` at 2 — two payment rows share one key, because each failed attempt commits its own row in its own transaction while the booking transaction (and its idempotency_record row) rolls back. Putting a unique constraint here would break the deliberate fail->retry->succeed drill. The idempotency guard lives on idempotency_record, not here.

columns.name: pending_at
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 happy path step 1 ('Insert a payment row in pending') · S-PAY-05 · S-SCP-12 ('pending_at <= authorized_at <= captured_at')
columns.note: The row is always created in pending, so this is always set.

columns.name: authorized_at
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 happy path step 3 ('Transition to authorized, then to captured, recording each timestamp') · S-PAY-05 · S-SCP-12
columns.note: Null while pending and on a failed row that never authorised. American spelling `authorized` throughout the documents (matching the enum value), not `authorised`.

columns.name: captured_at
columns.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 happy path step 3 · S-PAY-05 ('SELECT state, captured_at FROM payment WHERE id=P still returns pending and null')
columns.note: Null unless the row reached captured. Likely the source of EP-TKT-01's `paid_at` wire field — see gaps[].

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: E8 P-XCT-04 ('Every table carries created_at') · S-XCT-09
columns.note: Required by the blanket rule even though pending_at will normally hold the same instant.

checks.name: ck_payment__state
checks.cite: E3 P-PAY-07 · FR-ADR-041 · E7 P-RPT-03 ('payment.state is one of pending, authorized, captured, failed') · S-PAY-11 ('SELECT unnest(enum_range(NULL::payment_state))') · S-SCP-12 ('the column is state')
checks.why: the payment_state vocabulary. A CHECK rather than a PostgreSQL enum so that adding a value is an ordinary migration.

indexes.why: Every takings and dashboard aggregate filters `p.state = 'captured'`.
indexes.name: ix_payment__state

tables.name: receipt_dispatch
tables.purpose: One durable claim-and-outcome row per booking recording whether the receipt email was claimed, sent, failed or suppressed — the guard that makes two senders for one booking impossible, and the only record of what SES was asked to do.
tables.cite: FR-ADR-032 Decision; E4 P-TKT-05 'Send exactly one receipt per booking, and retry the ones that fail' Preconditions

columns.name: id
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 happy path step 2 (the claim UPDATE ends `RETURNING id`)
columns.note: THE TYPE IS NOT STATED. Same evidence and same caveat as outbox_message.id — see gaps. The claim returns it; nothing else in any document reads or joins on it.

columns.name: booking_id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-032 Decision ('A `receipt_dispatch` claim row, unique on `booking_id`'); E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions; Bible S-PAY-07
columns.note: TYPE IS FORCED BY A CRITERION'S SQL: S-PAY-07 runs `... WHERE r.booking_id = (o.payload->>'booking_id')::bigint`, so this column and booking.id must both be bigint or that test cannot run. This is the one hard type fact in this cluster.

columns.name: status
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions ('`status` (`pending` / `sending` / `sent` / `failed` / `suppressed`)'); E4 P-TKT-04 'The `suppressed` state' block; E4 P-TKT-10 state table
columns.note: FIVE values. Created `pending` by the booking transaction; `suppressed` is written ONLY by the seed script and by nothing in the running application, has no incoming edge from any other state and no outgoing edge at all (P-TKT-05 state machine). `sent` means SES ACCEPTED the message for delivery and is never revised — P-TKT-11: 'evidence of dispatch, never of receipt'. Modelled as text + CHECK; no document mandates a native enum.

columns.name: dispatch_seq
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions ('`dispatch_seq` (integer, `>= 1`)'); E4 P-TKT-04 happy path step 1 and Server-side validation; E4 P-TKT-07 happy path step 5; S8 merge report row X-10
columns.note: BUILD-SESSION EXTENSION, EXPLICITLY FLAGGED FOR 06 DataModel TO CONFIRM. It is the reconciliation of FR-ADR-032 (a `sent` claim is not retryable) against FR-ADR-048 (a resend control that re-enqueues the job): one row per booking stays unique on booking_id, and the worker's claim is conditional on the sequence so a stale redelivery cannot re-send. E4 lane notes: 'The merge pass and `06 DataModel` must confirm both, and if either is rejected the resend control needs a different mechanism.' Written 1 in the booking transaction; incremented only by an accepted resend.

columns.name: claimed_at
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions and happy path step 2 (`claimed_at=now()` in the claim UPDATE, and `claimed_at < now() - :stale_interval` in its WHERE)
columns.note: THE WORKER'S CLAIM COLUMN. Null on a row the booking transaction just created ('every timestamp null', P-TKT-04 step 1). IT IS NOT CLEARED ON FAILURE — unlike password_reset_token.email_claimed_at, which P-TKT-12 exception 4 clears to NULL explicitly. A failed receipt send moves status to 'failed' and leaves claimed_at set; the 'failed' branch of the claim's WHERE clause is what makes it retryable. Bible S-TKT-07 requires claimed_at to be written from the INJECTED clock and the staleness threshold bound from the same clock, asserting `rg -n 'now\(\)|CURRENT_TIMESTAMP' backend/app/workers` returns 0 hits — see notes, this contradicts the literal `now()` in the PRD's published claim statement.

columns.name: sent_at
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 happy path step 5 ('`sent_at=now()`'); E4 P-TKT-04 'The `suppressed` state' block
columns.note: Set only when SES accepted. Never cleared. Bible S-TKT-08 asserts it reads null on a timed-out send.

columns.name: ses_message_id
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions and happy path step 5 ('`ses_message_id=<the id SES returned>`'); FR-ADR-032 Consequences; FR-ADR-060
columns.note: The id SES returned on acceptance. FR-ADR-060: it 'is what makes "did this send" answerable'. Null on failure, on timeout and on a suppressed row.

columns.name: attempts
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions and happy path step 2 ('`attempts=attempts+1`'); E4 P-TKT-04 happy path step 1 ('`attempts = 0`')
columns.note: Written 0 in the booking transaction; no DB default stated. LOAD-BEARING BEYOND COUNTING: P-TKT-07 steps 3 and 4 use attempts=0 versus attempts>0 to distinguish 'the first receipt has not been attempted yet' (202 queued:false, no token spent) from 'a resend is already in flight' (202 queued:false). It is 0 only on a row no worker has ever claimed.

columns.name: last_error
columns.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions, exception rows 2 and 2a; FR-ADR-049 dimension 5
columns.note: Carries the SES error. MUST DISTINGUISH A TIMEOUT FROM A REFUSAL: P-TKT-05 exception 2a — 'last_error records that the call timed out rather than that SES refused, so the two are distinguishable afterwards by the operator'. Bible S-TKT-08 tests exactly that: last_error contains 'timeout' and does not contain the SES refusal string, and an SES error is 'distinguishable from the timeout case by that string'.

unique.cite: FR-ADR-032 Decision ('A `receipt_dispatch` claim row, unique on `booking_id`'); E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions ('unique on `booking_id`'); Bible S-TKT-05
unique.why: One row per booking is the whole guarantee. S-TKT-05: 'a second `receipt_dispatch` insert for the same booking_id does not commit and SELECT count(*) FROM receipt_dispatch WHERE booking_id=:b stays at 1.' The resend raises dispatch_seq on the same row rather than inserting a second, precisely so this constraint survives FR-ADR-048.
unique.name: uq_receipt_dispatch__booking_id

foreign_keys.cite: FR-ADR-032 Decision; FR-ADR-012 ('every relationship is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`. A cascade is a delete that happens without anyone writing the word delete')
foreign_keys.note: FR-ADR-012 fixes the action product-wide; no row in this cluster is ever deleted.
foreign_keys.name: fk_receipt_dispatch__booking_id

checks.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions; E4 P-TKT-04 'The `suppressed` state' block
checks.why: Closed five-member vocabulary, enumerated identically in three P-rows and proved complete as a 5x3 state machine in P-TKT-05. No criterion asserts the constraint itself, so the mechanism is open as it is for outbox_message.topic.
checks.name: ck_receipt_dispatch__1

checks.cite: E4 P-TKT-05 Preconditions ('`dispatch_seq` (integer, `>= 1`)'); E4 P-TKT-04 Server-side validation ('`dispatch_seq`: integer, `>= 1`')
checks.why: Stated twice as a bound on the value, in two separate specifications. A 0 or negative sequence would make the worker's sequence-conditional claim meaningless.
checks.name: ck_receipt_dispatch__2

tables.name: seat

columns.name: id
columns.cite: EP-ADM-20 path_params `seat_id: integer, positive`; EP-ADM-18/19 body `array of {id, row_label, seat_number, grid_row, grid_col, seat_category_id, is_active}`; E1 P-BRW-08 wire example `{"id": 4821, ...}`

columns.name: screen_id
columns.cite: P-ADM-13 (identity is (screen_id, row_label, seat_number)) · FR-ADR-016 · S-ADM-06 (`SELECT count(*) FROM seat WHERE screen_id = :id`) · P-ADM-14 (`INSERT INTO showtime_seat (showtime_id, seat_id) SELECT :showtime_id, id FROM seat WHERE screen_id = :screen_id AND is_active = true`)
columns.note: Seats belong to the screen, not to a showtime. Every seat write first takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on THIS screen row (P-ADM-13, P-ADM-14, P-ADM-15) — a build-session judgment call, stricter than any source, asserted by a pg_locks test in S-ADM-06.

columns.name: row_label
columns.cite: P-ADM-13 validation table · FR-ADR-016 · EP-ADM-19 / EP-ADM-20 request bodies · S-ADM-06 · S-ADM-07
columns.note: 1..4 characters, letters only. TWO reserved questions sit on this one column and they are different questions; NEITHER may be expressed as a CHECK, a citext type, a lower()/upper() expression index, or a normalising trigger. (a) CASE — OPEN-SEATLABEL-01: whether C12 and c12 are one seat or two. CONSTITUTION.md line 436 states the current position in terms: 'row_label is unique per screen and unnormalised'. The unique index below is therefore on the RAW column. Note the contradiction inside the PRD: P-ADM-13's validation table says 'stored uppercase' while its own prose two paragraphs later says the row decides nothing about case or normalisation, and journey defect J-ADM-09 (blocks-code) records exactly this and was resolved as 'open-article-x — only the client may answer it'. The Bible's S-ADM-06 description says its criteria 'normalise no case and ban no letter'. Implement no normalisation. (b) ALPHABET — OPEN-SEATALPHA-01 / PROPOSED-SEATALPHA-01: whether the letter I may appear at all. The seed skips I (rows run A B C D E F G H J K L M) because I and 1 are misread on a row marker; P-ADM-13's bound refuses nothing and EP-ADM-19/20 accept row I exactly as they accept row J. No CHECK, no regex beyond 'letters only'. (c) DEADLINE — P-ADM-14 freezes row_label the moment ANY showtime row exists on the screen, so a rule the client gives later cannot repair a row already written; the seed's 720 showtime inserts close that window on all six halls at once.

WHERE screen_id = :screen_id AND is_active = true` — and it is emphatically NOT the occupancy denominator (E7:373-374 forbids computing it from seat.is_active). tables.name: seat_category
tables.purpose: The priced seat band a seat belongs to: a lookup ROW (never a PostgreSQL enum) carrying the integer basis-point uplift applied uniformly to every hall's and every show's base price.
tables.cite: FR-ADR-016 (Decision: 'Categories: a `seat_category` lookup table, not a database enum'); P-ADM-11 (E6_admin.md, 'Set a seat category's percentage uplift, uniform across every hall and every show'); FR-ADR-037

columns.name: id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-017 (APPROVED): 'Primary keys are `bigint` identity columns — `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` — on every table.'
columns.note: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY. No application-generated id and no uuid: FR-ADR-017 rejects UUIDv4, UUIDv7/ULID, integer, a parallel public uuid column, and natural keys, each by name. The API contract spells this field 'integer' on the wire (EP-ADM-12/13/14 response bodies) — that is JSON typing, not a storage type, and does not contradict bigint.

columns.name: name
columns.cite: P-ADM-11 + SCR-ADM-04 ('Category name … 1..40 characters, unique on `lower(trim(name))`'); EP-ADM-13 request body ('string, 1..40 after trimming, unique on lower(trim(name)) (P-ADM-11), required')
columns.note: Bound is 1..40 AFTER trimming — narrower than the four vocabularies' 1..60. Stored as the admin typed it, case preserved, with only leading/trailing whitespace trimmed; the lowercased trimmed form is the comparison key and is never displayed (P-ADM-23, worked example). Seat category names Standard / Premium / Recliner are ASSUMED, never a constraint.

columns.name: uplift_basis_points
columns.cite: FR-ADR-037 ('The uplift is stored as an integer number of basis points, `uplift_basis_points`, where one basis point is 0.01%. 12.5% is `1250`.'); P-ADM-11; S-ADM-13
columns.note: MONEY-ADJACENT AND NEVER A FLOAT: FR-ADR-037 rejects `numeric` percentage by name because it 'puts a non-integer type on the money path'. **bigint, not integer, and this is load-bearing**: S-ADM-13 asserts the value 368934881464190 (~3.7e14) is ACCEPTED — that overflows PostgreSQL `integer` (2^31-1). The PRD prose calls the field 'integer' generically; the criterion that will be run requires 64-bit storage. Standard is a row whose uplift happens to be 0 and is NOT a special case in code (FR-ADR-037; S-ADM-13 asserts ripgrep for `uplift_basis_points == 0|if not uplift|Standard` in pricing.py returns 0 hits). Seeded values 0 / 1250 / 3333 are ASSUMED (P-XCT-30).

columns.name: version
columns.cite: FR-ADR-035 ('Two admins editing the same row: optimistic concurrency with a `version` integer … This applies to `movie`, `showtime`, `screen` and `seat_category`.'); S-ADM-14; E6_admin.md 'Optimistic concurrency and the VERSION_CONFLICT path'
columns.note: S-ADM-14 runs a literal catalogue query asserting the set of tables carrying `version` is EXACTLY {movie, showtime, screen, seat_category, cinema}. seat_category is IN that set; the four vocabulary tables below are NOT. EP-ADM-13's 201 body returns version '1', so a new row starts at 1; a successful write increments by exactly 1; a no-op write does not increment. Whether the 1 is a database DEFAULT or set by the application is not stated anywhere — see gaps.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: P-XCT-04 precondition: 'Every table carries `created_at`; tables that mutate carry `updated_at`.'; S-XCT-09 (literal catalogue query asserting zero tables lack created_at)
columns.note: NO DATABASE-SIDE DEFAULT. No now(), no CURRENT_TIMESTAMP — time is injected (FR-ADR-018, CONSTITUTION Art IX.5). The application supplies the instant from the injected clock.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.cite: P-XCT-04 precondition: 'Every table carries `created_at`; tables that mutate carry `updated_at`.'; S-XCT-09 Description: 'tables that are edited after creation are expected to carry updated_at as well as created_at; which tables those are is a judgement that follows from the data model and is checked there rather than here.'
columns.note: seat_category mutates (EP-ADM-14 changes name and uplift), so the P-XCT-04 rule reaches it. Nullable because no document says what the value is before the first edit; S-XCT-09 explicitly delegates the decision to the data model. See gaps — the merge owner must settle null-until-first-edit vs equal-to-created_at. No clock default here either.

unique.cite: P-ADM-23 ('Every name this epic makes unique is unique on `lower(trim(name))`: a **seat category** (`P-ADM-11`) …, enforced by a unique index and not by a prior read'); S-ADM-13 ('A name colliding on lower(trim(name)) returns 422 with A seat category with that name already exists.'); EP-ADM-13 idempotency note ('A repeat fails with VALIDATION_FAILED on the unique index over lower(trim(name))')

The reason reaches the customer here and not only the admin: the category is the primary non-colour carrier of price band on the seat map, so `Premium` and `premium` coexisting would draw two legend rows on every seat map for what a customer reads as one category (P-ADM-23).

checks.cite: PRD field-bound table for P-ADM-11: '`uplift_basis_points` | integer | `>= 0` | **derived** — a negative uplift is a discount, and `SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-02` rules out discount codes, concession pricing and every other reduction (`FR-ADR-040`)'; S-ADM-13 ('-1 returns 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with The uplift cannot be negative. This system has no discounts.')

checks.cite: SCR-ADM-04 fields table ('1..40 characters'); EP-ADM-13/EP-ADM-14 request body; P-ADM-11. Provenance is marked **technical** in the PRD's own provenance scheme — a storage bound chosen by the build session, not a business figure.

tables.name: showtime

tables.cite: P-ADM-07 (docs/03 PRD/sections/E6_admin.md S4); FR-ADR-018; FR-ADR-022; FR-ADR-037

columns.name: id
columns.cite: FR-ADR-017
columns.note: Public and enumerable on purpose — FR-ADR-017: 'Knowing that showtime 41 exists discloses nothing; the seat map for it is already public to guests.' Scrapeability is handled by rate limiting, not authorisation.

columns.name: movie_id
columns.cite: P-ADM-07 validation table; EP-ADM-10
columns.note: The film NEED NOT BE PUBLISHED — a showtime may be scheduled against a draft (S-ADM-09 asserts 201 against a movie whose published_at is null). Editable on PATCH (EP-ADM-11 accepts movie_id).

columns.name: screen_id
columns.cite: P-ADM-07 validation table; P-ADM-09
columns.note: IMMUTABLE after creation. A PATCH carrying a different screen_id is 422 — 'Moving a showtime to another hall would move every existing booking onto seats that may not exist in the new hall.' Build-session judgment, Art III.9, stricter so unsigned. Screen must be is_active at create (409 LAYOUT_FROZEN otherwise).

columns.name: starts_at
columns.cite: P-ADM-07 validation table; FR-ADR-018; SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01
columns.note: The advertised start, stored as a UTC INSTANT. Accepted and returned as a NAIVE LOCAL Asia/Kolkata string on the admin API; a value carrying Z, an offset or a zone name is 422 and is NEVER coerced. Serialised WITH the cinema's +05:30 offset on every customer surface. The zone is read from the cinema row, never from CINEMA_TIMEZONE at request time — S-ADM-04 asserts information_schema returns 0 columns matching '%timezone%' on showtime and screen, 'so a showtime reaches its zone only as showtime to screen to cinema.timezone'.

columns.name: ends_at
columns.cite: P-ADM-07 validation table; S-ACC-12
columns.note: STORED, never derived from movie.runtime_minutes. S-ACC-12 asserts SELECT is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='showtime' AND column_name='ends_at' returns NO. Strictly after starts_at in the MERGED row on a PATCH. Half-open interval [starts_at, ends_at) for the overlap predicate.

columns.name: base_price_paise
columns.cite: P-ADM-10; P-PAY-03 exception 1; FR-ADR-037; SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01
columns.note: MONEY, INTEGER PAISE. P-PAY-03 exception 1: 'The column is bigint NOT NULL with no default, so the row cannot be created.' S-SEA-16 asserts schema.sql declares bigint for exactly showtime.base_price_paise, booking_seat.price_paise, booking_seat.base_price_paise_applied and booking.total_paise. That the price sits PER SHOWTIME rather than once globally is PROVISIONAL under SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-01 / FR-ADR-037 — reversing it moves this column to a configuration value and backfills. Bound >= 1 at the admin write (P-ADM-10); P-PAY-03's pricing function separately states >= 0 — see notes.

columns.name: format_id
columns.cite: P-ADM-07 ('Format sits on the showtime, not on the film'); EP-ADM-10; EP-ADM-11
columns.note: OPTIONAL — 'one film runs 2D in one hall and 3D in another on the same day'. Null answers null on the browse surface and is EXCLUDED by any format filter. Must name an ACTIVE format row at write time; a showtime already carrying a withdrawn format keeps it. PATCH accepts null to clear it. This is the only place showtime.format_id is written.

columns.name: seat_count_at_creation
columns.cite: P-ADM-14 (E6_admin.md, 'A showtime's seat set is materialised when the showtime is created'); FR-ADR-022

S-ADM-08 asserts SELECT count(*) FROM showtime s WHERE s.seat_count_at_creation <> (SELECT count(*) FROM showtime_seat ss WHERE ss.showtime_id = s.id) returns 0. Creating a showtime on a screen with zero in-service seats is 409 LAYOUT_FROZEN, 'so no showtime can carry a zero denominator'.

columns.note: Application-set to 1 on insert, +1 per successful write. Unchanged by a no-op. In S-ADM-14's exact five-table set.

tables.name: users
tables.purpose: One row per person who holds an account — customer, manager or admin; the identity every booking, audit row and reset token points at.
tables.cite: P-ACC-01 (E5 S4, 'The complete field list of the user row') · E8 S7.5 · FR-ADR-050

columns.name: id
columns.cite: P-ACC-09 — 'booking.user_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT'; EP-ADM-22/EP-ADM-23 return user_id as 'integer'; P-XCT-03's worked example uses actor_user_id 17
columns.note: INTEGER, not uuid. Three documents spell the referencing column `integer`, so the brief's uuid default does not apply here. NO DOCUMENT STATES THE GENERATION MECHANISM (identity column vs sequence) — audit_log is the only table where a document says 'identity'.

columns.name: email
columns.cite: P-ACC-01 step 5 and its validation table · E8 S7.5 · P-XCT-06 preconditions
columns.note: Stored AS ENTERED, 3..254 characters after trimming. Uniqueness is a unique index on `lower(email)` — E8 S7.5 explicitly refuses a second lowercased column ('two fields to keep in step'), so this is NOT citext and NOT a stored lowercase column. Written once by P-ACC-01 and never updated by anything (S-ACC-06 asserts the mapper's changed-attribute set never contains `email`).

columns.name: password_hash
columns.cite: P-ACC-01 (field table: `text`, NOT NULL) · P-ACC-03 (bcrypt, BCRYPT_COST default 12) · S-ACC-02
columns.note: bcrypt. The ALGORITHM IS NAMED BY THE DOCUMENTS (P-ACC-03: 'Algorithm bcrypt'; E8 S7.5; FR-ADR-050) — nothing is inferred. NOT NULL on every row without exception: a manager account with no usable password carries a real bcrypt digest of 32 discarded CSPRNG bytes, drawn PER ROW so two such rows never share a value (S-ACC-02 asserts count(*) - count(DISTINCT password_hash) = 0 over rows with last_signed_in_at IS NULL). A nullable column is refused by name, because a null test before the verification is the early return P-ACC-03's timing property forbids.

columns.name: role
columns.cite: S3.1 'The four roles' (Modelled as: `user.role = 'customer'` / `'manager'` / `'admin'`) · P-XCT-05 preconditions ('exactly one role value in a single column') · FR-ADR-009 · SRC-003 C-1
columns.note: PROVISIONAL that the manager value exists at all (SRC-003 C-1). Roles are mutually exclusive, one column, never a many-to-many table (S3.1, FR-ADR-050). Set to 'customer' by the application at registration and to 'manager' by P-ADM-17; NO ENDPOINT EVER CREATES 'admin' (S-ADM-18 asserts every /api/admin POST and PUT leaves the admin count unchanged and that `role = 'admin'` appears only in scripts/seed.py). NO DOCUMENT STATES THE DATABASE REPRESENTATION — see gaps. closed vocabulary, enforced by a CHECK rather than a PostgreSQL enum type

columns.name: password_version
columns.cite: P-ACC-05 ('an integer starting at 1 and incremented on every password change') · P-ACC-01 step 5 · P-ACC-08 step 4
columns.note: THE SESSION-INVALIDATION COUNTER. It is the JWT's `pv` claim; the authorisation dependency loads the user row by primary key on every authenticated request and rejects the token when `pv` does not match this column (P-ACC-05 exception 4). Written as 1 by the application at insert — no document states a database default. Incremented by P-ACC-08 only: `password_version = password_version + 1`.

columns.name: created_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-01 step 5 · FR-ADR-018 ('`created_at` and `updated_at` are `timestamptz` and default to `now()` at the database') · EP-ADM-22 returns it
columns.note: Required on every table in the schema — S-XCT-09 asserts that no table in `public` other than `alembic_version` lacks a `created_at`.

columns.name: last_signed_in_at
columns.cite: P-ACC-01 (field table: timestamptz, UTC, nullable) · P-ACC-02 step 4 · P-ACC-08 step 4
columns.note: NULL means the account has never signed in — a real and expected state, not a defect. Written from the INJECTED CLOCK on every successful sign-in (`UPDATE users SET last_signed_in_at = :now WHERE id = :id`) and inside P-ACC-08's reset transaction. NOT written on a failed attempt. `has_signed_in` on EP-ADM-22 is DERIVED as `last_signed_in_at IS NOT NULL` and is never stored (S-ADM-18 asserts no `has_signed_in` column exists in information_schema).

unique.cite: P-ACC-01 step 3 · P-XCT-06 preconditions ('A unique index exists on `lower(email)`') · E8 S7.5
unique.why: Email is the identity, unique case-insensitively. It is an EXPRESSION index, not a column constraint — a second lowercased column is refused by name in S7.5. It is the guard, not a prior read: P-ACC-01 step 6 catches the unique violation and translates it to 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED, and S-ACC-01 asserts 20 simultaneous identical registrations produce exactly 1 success and 19 conflicts with no 500.
unique.name: uq_users__email_ci
